findings.current: *You picked a fine day to die.*
findings.defect: The draft adds an explicit threat to kill Taekyung. The source only conveys that Mukyung has caught him at an opportune moment to punish him.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves Mukyung’s punitive intent without inventing a death threat.

findings.current:
“What happened to you? Did you drink some kind of stone oil?”

“Why would I drink oil? You’re completely insane.”
findings.defect: The draft turns 공청석유, a named elixir, into generic “stone oil” and therefore obscures the homophone joke behind Taekyung’s response.
findings.rationale: Transliteration retains the named item, while the footnote makes the source’s petroleum misunderstanding intelligible without inserting an explanation into the dialogue.
findings.replacement:
“What happened to you? Did you drink *gongcheong seokyu*[^2] or something?”

“Why would I drink oil? You’re completely insane.”

[^2]: *Gongcheong seokyu* is a rare martial-arts elixir; *seokyu* is also the Korean word for petroleum.
findings.source:
“어떻게 된 거지? 공청석유라도 마셨나?”

“석유를 왜 마셔. 이거 완전히 미친놈이네.”

findings.current: “Hyung. I don’t think that’s quite fair.”
findings.defect: 형님 is markedly more deferential than 형. Taekyung abruptly raises his register once Mukyung releases his full power, but the draft repeats the casual address and loses that comic submission.
findings.rationale: The deferential form preserves the deliberate register shift and the brothers’ hierarchy.
findings.replacement: “Hyung-nim. I don’t think that’s quite fair.”

findings.defect: 시벌 is a deliberately distorted or minced form of the stronger 씨발. The draft makes the euphemistic profanity fully explicit.
findings.rationale: The replacement remains profane and exasperated without erasing the source’s softened comic form.

findings.defect: The action is reversed. Soyul is not apologizing; she sternly demands that Taekyung acknowledge that he did wrong by covering her with the blanket.
findings.rationale: The replacement restores Soyul as the accuser and preserves her childish speech.

findings.defect: The source describes a smile, not audible laughter.
findings.rationale: 배시시 웃다 denotes a small, pleased smile; changing it to a giggle alters the physical action.

findings.current: Only then did the door open cautiously. Socheon spoke with an apologetic expression.
findings.defect: 황송하다 conveys deferential gratitude and humility toward someone greatly honored, not an apology. The draft loses Socheon’s hierarchical reverence for his Benefactor.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves Socheon’s deferential register and emotional posture.
findings.replacement: Only then did the door cautiously open. Looking deeply humbled, Socheon said,
findings.source: 그제야 방문이 조심스럽게 열렸다. 소천이 황송하다는 얼굴로 말했다.

findings.current:
“Big brother’s part of it too!”

“He must be in on it.”
findings.defect: The draft removes Soyul’s childish malapropism: she says 한 무더기, “a whole heap,” instead of 한패, “one of the same gang.” It also turns Taekyung’s correction into an ordinary interpretation.
findings.rationale: The replacement restores both the mistaken word and Taekyung’s deadpan correction.
findings.replacement:
“Big brother’s a whole heap too!”

“You mean he’s in on it.”

findings.current: If she had been some black-haired male, I could have beaten her senseless without worrying about social criticism or pangs of conscience.
findings.defect: 시커먼 사내놈 does not describe black hair. It disparagingly evokes a full-grown, rough male; the draft invents a hair-color detail and retains a feminine pronoun after the imagined sex change.
findings.rationale: The replacement restores the contemptuous physical characterization and keeps the counterfactual pronouns coherent.
findings.replacement: If she were some hulking bastard of a man, I could beat him senseless without worrying about social criticism or pangs of conscience.
findings.source: 시커먼 사내놈이라면 사회적 비판이나 양심의 가책 없이 뒤지게 팰 수 있을 테니까.

findings.current:
They say you’re a shoo-in to become the next head of the Gatekeepers.”

“T-The next head of the Gatekeepers!”
findings.defect: 수문각주 is the formal title for the master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion, not merely a generic head of the gatekeepers. The draft obscures the institutional post and Hyuk Mujin’s prospective promotion from Captain.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves the distinct office, organization, and hierarchical promotion.
findings.replacement:
They say you’re a shoo-in to become the next Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion.”

“T-The next Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion!”
findings.source:
차기 수문각주는 따 놓은 당상이라던데.

“수, 수문각주!”

findings.current: “He was strong. I, the next head of the Gatekeepers, fought him for more than a hundred exchanges without either of us managing to win…”
findings.defect: The later repetition again substitutes a generic leadership description for the formal office 수문각주, making Hyuk Mujin’s boast terminologically inconsistent with his actual promotion.
findings.rationale: The replacement keeps the formal title consistent and preserves the boast that even someone of Hyuk Mujin’s newly claimed stature could not decide the contest.
findings.replacement: “He was strong. Even I, the next Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion, fought him for more than a hundred exchanges without settling the match…”
findings.source: “강한 놈이었지. 차기 수문각주인 내가 백여 합을 겨뤘지만 승부를 보지 못할 정도로…….”

summary: One reversed action, several lost register and wordplay cues, an added death threat, and localized terminology errors require correction.
